standard_prerequisites.name: Divisors supported on the special fibre, the intersection pairing and the additivity of the Euler characteristic
standard_prerequisites.statement: The situation fixes a discrete valuation ring, a smooth projective curve over its fraction field, a regular proper model and the components of the special fibre with their multiplicities; a divisor supported on the special fibre is a nonnegative combination of its components, the degree pairing of a combination of components against an invertible sheaf is symmetric, and for an effective Cartier divisor the structure sheaf of the sum of two summands fits into a short exact sequence comparing it with the sheaves of the summands and of their intersection. The Euler characteristic of a coherent sheaf on a proper scheme over a field is additive in short exact sequences, and the intersection numbers of the components are read off from the numerical type. The author's own notions and the quoted results of the Divisors, Morphisms and Varieties chapters are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the bookkeeping step used in the genus formula of the section: it computes how the invariants change when one component is added to a divisor supported on the special fibre.

core_obligations: Compare the two divisors: the difference between the larger divisor and the smaller one is the single component, and the structure sheaf of the larger divisor fits into the short exact sequence comparing it with the sheaves of the smaller divisor and of the component, which is the chapter's description of a sum of effective Cartier divisors together with the standard short exact sequence for a regular section (source lines 5124-5140).

Compute the correction to the intersection pairing: the degree pairing of the added component against the other components is symmetric, so the intersection numbers of the larger divisor are those of the smaller one shifted by the intersection numbers of the added component (source lines 5140-5148).

Read off the change in the genus: the additivity of the Euler characteristic applied to the short exact sequence expresses the change of the genus of the divisor in terms of the numerical invariants of the added component, namely its residue field, its genus and its self-intersection number, which is the assertion of the statement (source lines 5148-5154).

proof_roadmap.step: Write down the short exact sequence comparing the two divisors.
Compute the shift in the intersection pairing caused by the added component.
Apply the additivity of the Euler characteristic to express the change of the genus.
